meta.title: The Waiting List
meta.standfirst: A public, dated record of a DFFH Priority Access housing complaint — the facts, the timeline, and the pattern of other people hitting the same wall.

pages.title: Overview
pages.body:
This page exists because a single complaint is easy to dismiss and a pattern is not. It's a dated, factual record of a Priority Access housing application with Victoria's Department of Families, Fairness and Housing, kept in one place, updated as things change, and built to be handed to anyone who needs the whole picture at once: a journalist, an MP's office, or the Victorian Ombudsman.

Application
7105877341, effective 7 April 2026, approved 20 August 2026, with entitlement assessed at one bedroom only. A priority transfer process was already under way in April 2025, twelve months before that effective date. See the timeline.
Outcome
The department has refused the request for the two-bedroom property, stating it is scheduled for extensive maintenance before being offered to the two-bedroom wait list. No scheduled date has been given and no vacancy duration has been stated by the department. The stated position is that a single applicant is entitled to a one bedroom property regardless.
Complaint
CM0079923. A written response dated 20 August 2026 was received by email on 21 August 2026. It confirms the application is approved for a one-bedroom property and refuses the request for the two-bedroom property, stating that the property is scheduled to undergo extensive maintenance and will then be offered to applicants on the two-bedroom wait list. It does not state how long the property has been vacant. See Status and next steps.
Housing history
No fixed address since 22 April 2025, sixteen months. Six placements, none provided by the department. Currently residing in a caravan, Koroit. A DFFH tenancy at Port Fairy ran from February to April 2025 and ended when a court order barred entry to the property.
The property in question
A property in Koroit, occupied for approximately three years until February 2025, vacant since. The property has appeared unoccupied since February 2025. That is an observation from the record kept here, not a departmental figure. The department has not stated a vacancy duration. During the occupancy that ended in February 2025 the department arranged a substantial programme of maintenance at the property. See the timeline. Address withheld to protect nearby family members' privacy.
Today
21 August 2026. Victorian Ombudsman referral proceeding, the departmental window having closed unresolved. A meeting with the department has been offered for today.
Separate matter, evidenced
$1,038.80 was deducted from a Disability Support Pension and paid to the department as rent for the Port Fairy property across eleven weeks after a court order barred entry to it. Not refunded, not explained. See the timeline.
Share your own story

Why this exists

Individually, delays like this are easy for a system to treat as one person's bad luck. Since going public, this hasn't looked like one person's bad luck, see The Pattern for other people's accounts of the same wait, the same system, in their own words.

pages.title: Timeline
pages.body:
• Feb 2025
    Left a property in Koroit after approximately three years. No secure accommodation since. The property has remained vacant. (Address withheld here to protect nearby family members' privacy, the same standard applied to the public Facebook post.)
  • 2022-2025
    During the occupancy that ended in February 2025, the department arranged and completed a substantial programme of maintenance at the property. The works included a reverse cycle heating and cooling unit, a new shower, repainted walls, laundry repairs, tap replacement, smoke alarm replacement and plumbing repairs. Grounds were kept under a regular contracted mowing service. This is an account from the occupancy, not a departmental record. The department holds the maintenance history for the property and it would settle the point either way.
  • Feb-Apr 2025
    Assisted transition from Koroit arranged by Brophy Tenancy Plus into a DFFH tenancy at Port Fairy. That tenancy ended in April 2025. No fixed address since.
  • 29-30 Apr 2025
    A priority transfer was already in progress. A Salvation Army caseworker requested documents in support of it on 29 April 2025, and thirteen were provided the following day. Correspondence held. The department's recorded effective date for the current application is 7 April 2026, twelve months later.
  • 22 Apr 2025
    A court order took effect barring entry to the Port Fairy property. No fixed address from this date.
  • 27 May - 8 Jul 2025
    Rent continued to be deducted from a Disability Support Pension for that property for eleven weeks after the exclusion took effect. Centrelink records show $259.70 per fortnight paid to the Department of Families, Fairness and Housing across four fortnights, an evidenced total of $1,038.80, ending 8 July 2025. Across the same period $600 a fortnight was being paid for motel accommodation from the same pension. A Centrelink statement dated 26 May 2025 was still addressed to the Port Fairy property five weeks after the exclusion. No refund has been made and no explanation given. Earlier payments fall outside Centrelink's fifteen-month online window, so the true total may be higher. Only the evidenced figure is claimed.
  • 22 Jul 2025
    Deduction ceased without notice. Full gross pension paid from this date.
  • 7 Apr 2026
    Priority Access application lodged. Reference 7105877341.
  • 6 Aug 2026
    Jacinta Ermacora MP (Member for Western Victoria) contacted. No response to date.
  • 7-10 Aug 2026
    Sustained, escalating blood pressure readings, peaking at 228/149.
  • 12 Aug 2026
    Three-drug treatment regimen commenced under treating specialist. Specialist support letter completed and sent to DFFH, Salvos Connect, and Roma Britnell MP's office. Forwarded independently by Salvos caseworker.
  • 12 Aug 2026
    Roma Britnell MP (Member for South West Coast) responded, encouraging the application and confirming a ministerial representation was underway.
  • 13 Aug 2026
    Acute health episode, blood pressure to 195/123 with transient neurological-type symptoms, resolved without hospital presentation, following clinical guidance.
  • 14 Aug 2026
    Public post published to two local Facebook community groups. Substantial organic reach within hours, see Reach.
  • 14 Aug 2026
    Outreach sent to local media regarding the housing situation specifically, as a follow-up to an earlier, broader approach made in June.
  • 14 Aug 2026
    This record published at mahda.com.au/waiting-list/, consolidating the timeline, health evidence, and the pattern of other people's accounts in one place, ahead of wider sharing.
  • 20 Aug 2026
    DFFH's stated complaint response window closed. Also the date of a previously scheduled echocardiogram.
  • 20 Aug 2026
    Two short videos posted publicly from outside the DFFH office, the same pattern as three prior visits with no update given.
  • 20 Aug 2026
    Approximately fifteen minutes after the second video was posted, a call was received from the department, the first substantive contact in this process. A follow-up email confirmed receipt of the 12 August specialist letter but did not answer the specific questions raised: the bedroom-entitlement policy, whether the property in question had been formally assessed, and the reason for its continued vacancy.
  • 20 Aug 2026
    Application 7105877341 confirmed approved. The department's position is that entitlement is to a one-bedroom property. The two-bedroom property this record concerns, previously occupied for three years, was confirmed by the department itself as vacant for eighteen months.
  • 20 Aug 2026
    Complaint window closed without the questions above being answered. Considered unresolved.
  • 21 Aug 2026 (scheduled)
    Victorian Ombudsman referral, now proceeding since the window closed unresolved. A meeting has also been offered with the department, in Warrnambool or via Salvos Connect.
  • 21 Aug 2026
    Written response to complaint CM0079923 received by email at 2.59pm, on a letter dated 20 August 2026 and signed by a Team Leader, Wimmera South West Area. It confirms approval for a one-bedroom property under a special housing needs priority category across Camperdown/Terang, Koroit, Port Fairy, Warrnambool or Portland. It refuses the request for the two-bedroom property on the basis that the property is scheduled to undergo extensive maintenance and will then be offered to eligible applicants on the two-bedroom wait list. No maintenance date is given and no vacancy duration is stated. The letter sets out an appeal pathway and refers to the Victorian Public Tenants Association.
  • 21 Aug 2026
    Commenting was disabled on the Koroit Community Notice Board post only. Existing comments remain visible, new replies are not possible. Posts in the two Warrnambool groups were unaffected and remain open. No explanation given. Disabling replies on a single post within a single group is an ordinary moderation control available to that group's administrators, and nothing here should be read as implying otherwise.
  • 21 Aug 2026
    Reach figures re-read from the platform's own analytics across the full 28-day window and published post by post, see Reach. The Pattern page extended with the public objections raised and the answers given.

pages.title: The pattern
pages.kicker: Other people, same system, their own words
pages.body:
The public post asked a simple question: if you've hit something similar with DFFH or Priority Access housing, say so. This is what came back — growing by the day. Presented as offered, in public community groups, first names as given, anonymous where that was the person's own choice.

Waiting to get in

Cathy
On the general waiting list over 10 years. Her son was recently rejected for priority housing. She continues working into her 70s to house him.
A parent, Hamilton
Daughter on the priority list 6 years. Told to expect a wait of 10-plus years.
John
Applied 3 years ago. No response despite repeated calls.
Fiona
On a single-unit list for 3 years, statewide. Told by phone that approximately 60,000 Victorians are currently on the waiting list. (Figure as reported to her; not yet independently verified — see note below, and see Documented Cases for a separate, sourced statewide figure that should not be confused with this one.)
Rebecca
On the Priority Access list 8 years. Told the specific hold-up is a shortage of one-bedroom properties, and that she has been declined a two-bedroom placement even as a priority applicant, on the reasoning that it might be needed by someone else.
Renata
On the list over 10 years, Warrnambool, specifically for a one-bedroom, under the mental health priority category, no children. Given the identical one-bedroom-shortage reasoning as Rebecca, independently. Says she has given up hope of being housed here. Two separate applicants describing the same official explanation is no longer an anecdote, it is a policy being described consistently from outside. Two more accounts have since described the same mechanism, one unprompted from the opposite side of the argument, see The objections below.
Anonymous
Medical priority lodged in 2014, after a serious illness ended her ability to work. In 2018, after a welfare check was requested by an NDIS advocate, the department discovered her application had never actually been lodged — it had been sitting in an office drawer the whole time. Once properly lodged, she was told a medical priority "means nothing" unless also fleeing family violence, a single parent, or dealing with addiction; a Geelong DFFH official told her directly, "you won't see housing in your lifetime." Fifty-eight private rental applications were declined between 2018 and COVID-19, despite the ability to pay rent and bond without government assistance. Earlier this year she discovered, by chance, in a spam folder, that she had been removed from the priority and housing lists entirely, on the assumption she must have found housing by now. She was reinstated only because she found the email and rang — the staff member who helped her apologised personally for the system.

Allocation that does not match its own rules

A separate strand, reported by others and not verified here: placements that appear to contradict the entitlement reasoning applied elsewhere.

Reported, unverified
A commenter stated they know of a single person housed in a three-bedroom property. Reported second-hand, with no detail offered and nothing verified. Recorded here only because it sits directly against the reasoning given to Rebecca and Renata, that a single applicant cannot be placed in a larger property because someone else may need it.
The mechanism, named directly
One commenter, speaking from direct experience with Homes Victoria, confirmed that room-sharing and informal transitional arrangements in public housing are actively breached, unauthorised occupants and renting a room to someone are both grounds for a breach. Taken together with the one-bedroom shortage described above, that leaves a declared relationship as the one form of household combination the system rewards rather than penalises. Offered as an explanation of how the rules work, not as a criticism.

Housed, but not safe

A different failure, worth keeping distinct from the wait itself: what happens after someone is finally placed.

Seth
Homeless and couch surfing for over 3 years before being housed. The property has ongoing structural movement, cracking walls, mould and water damage that recur after being reported as "fixed." Rent was raised to the maximum as soon as one of the two tenants' circumstances improved.
A commenter on emergency accommodation funding
Reported that Salvos-funded hotel accommodation for homeless families is generally capped around six weeks before families are without a placement again while reapplying. (Figure given as a rough impression by the commenter, not confirmed against a funding document.)

The objections

A record that publishes only the supportive replies is not a record. These are the objections raised publicly in the same threads, paraphrased, alongside the answers given at the time. Commenters are not named here. Several were argued in good faith and one of them improved this page.

"Be grateful. A roof is better than a tent."
No property has been refused at any point in this process. The question raised is not about deserving more, it is about a house that has served nobody for eighteen months.
"Get a job. Nobody owes you anything."
Self-employed, working full days. Effort is not the variable that determines whether an empty property is allocated.
"Find someone in the same situation and apply together."
Bedroom entitlement is assessed on household need, not on the number of names on a form. Two unrelated single applicants are not assessed as a household. A generous suggestion that does not survive contact with the policy.
"You qualified for a flat. A family on the two-bedroom list should get that house."
The strongest objection received, and it prompted a correction to this record. This is not a general request for a larger property ahead of a waiting family. It concerns the specific property occupied for approximately three years until February 2025, which has been vacant since. Whether that history creates any claim to that specific address is an open question, which is precisely why it sits in a formal complaint and an Ombudsman referral rather than being asserted as settled. The same commenter proposed the fix as either building far more one-bedroom stock or merging the one and two-bedroom lists, which is the same mechanism Rebecca and Renata were independently given as the reason for their own refusals.
"This is what a Labor government gets you."
A Liberal MP and a Labor MP are both engaged with this matter. A vacant property is vacant irrespective of who is in office, and this record is kept non-partisan.
"Give it to a family living in a car or a tent."
Agreed, and not in tension with anything on this page. The objection here is to the vacancy itself, not to who is eventually placed there. A house occupied by a family in need would resolve the complaint on its merits.
"Hard work and sacrifice is the only way out. I have been homeless three times."
Offered from real experience and taken seriously. It still does not describe a mechanism by which an individual's effort causes an unallocated property to be allocated.
"People stepping over each other to get ahead."
The property in question is not allocated to another applicant. It is empty. Nobody is displaced by asking why.
"Why did you give the property up?"
A common misreading worth correcting directly. The vacant property was left in February 2025 in circumstances that were not chosen. It has not been occupied by anyone since.
"Vacated properties often get trashed or contaminated, try widening your preferred areas."
A fair general point that carries no confirmation for this specific property. The department's letter states scheduled maintenance with no scope or date given. The current approval already spans five towns, this was never about one address over the whole region.
"More people expect government housing than is available, keep trying private rental."
Already housed by the department twice, and lost both, through a court order and a departmental decision, not through giving up on other options. Private rental on a Disability Support Pension in this region is largely closed, which is most of why Priority Access exists as a category.

A possible structural cause, unverified

One account offered a systemic explanation rather than a personal one, kept separate because it could not be verified to the same standard as the rest of this page.

Reported, partly corroborated
A DFFH housing tenant stated that most Victorian housing property managers left the department around November 2025, citing an inability to get anything done, and reported twelve months trying to get help herself without result. This cannot be confirmed for housing property managers specifically. What can be confirmed: a substantial Victorian Public Service job-cut round followed the Silver Review, originally proposed at up to 6,000 full-time roles and negotiated down to approximately 2,000, alongside an active union campaign that drew more than 1,500 members to a single meeting in December 2025. An understaffed team defaulting to standard reasons rather than individually assessing files is consistent with that broader picture, though not established as the specific cause here.

If your experience matches any of this, it belongs here too, see Share your story.

Some figures on this page — the 60,000 statewide waitlist number and the six-week hotel funding cap — were reported by other people in the thread from memory or hearsay, not sourced documents. They're kept separate from the independently sourced figures on the Documented Cases page. Worth verifying either before quoting them to a journalist, MP office, or the Ombudsman.

pages.title: Documented cases
pages.kicker: Independently reported, not just personal accounts
pages.body:
Everything on the Pattern page is testimony — real, but self-reported. This page is different: cases that have already been independently reported by local journalists, with names, dates and departmental responses on the record. It exists because independently verified cases carry weight the rest of this page can't claim on its own.

Doug Bowen — Warrnambool

A Warrnambool father raising his two children alone since his wife's death in 2019 — including his daughter Nova, who has cerebral palsy and uses a wheelchair — has been on the priority housing list for more than five years. Documented in The Warrnambool Standard, the family has at various points lived in a van, in motels, and couch-surfed, and has depended on temporary accommodation provided on a goodwill basis by a community member. Roma Britnell, the local Member for South West Coast, has advocated for the family for more than two years, including raising the case in State Parliament and personally visiting vacant DFFH properties in Warrnambool to verify the department's own vacancy claims. In one report, Mr Bowen said the department never physically met the family in six years to assess their situation in person.

Statewide figures, independently sourced

Average wait
Homeless Victorians now wait 20 months on average for housing to be found — double the government's own target time frame.
Homes needed
The government's own infrastructure expert has recommended Victoria urgently build 60,000 new social homes. This is a different figure from the 60,000-people-on-the-waitlist number reported elsewhere on this site — one is homes needed, the other is people waiting. They should not be conflated.

Source: The Warrnambool Standard, multiple reports 2024–2026. Figures current as reported at time of publication — worth confirming against the original articles before citing further.

pages.title: The health evidence
pages.body:
The argument this record makes isn't that bureaucratic delay is unpleasant. It's that this specific delay has coincided with a documented, escalating health event, and that the coincidence is now on the record with a treating specialist.

Diagnoses
Hypertensive cardiomyopathy, left ventricular hypertrophy, coronary microvascular dysfunction, chronic myocardial ischaemia. A 2019 angiogram excluded obstructive coronary disease.
Crisis readings
7–10 August 2026, peaking at 228/149, while unmedicated.
Treatment
Three-drug regimen commenced 12 August 2026 under a treating specialist at South West Healthcare.
Specialist letter
Completed 12 August 2026, supporting the housing application on medical grounds. Provided to DFFH, Salvos Connect, and the local MP's office.
13 August episode
A further acute rise to 195/123 with transient, one-sided neurological-type symptoms. Assessed against clinical guidance and did not require hospital presentation. Documented and reported to the treating specialist the same evening.

This section will be updated as further clinical detail becomes appropriate to make public. It is not a substitute for the full medical record, which is held privately.

The figures below are read directly from the platform's own Content Library analytics, in the platform's own 28-day window of 24 July to 21 August 2026, and are reproduced post by post so they can be checked rather than taken on trust.

Totals

Views
63,701 across the ten housing-related posts above. The two largest posts account for 47,016 of that total between them.
Engagements
17,749 combined likes, comments, shares and reactions. The single property post accounts for 11,812 of them.
Viewers
The per-post viewer counts sum to 35,487, but this is not a count of unique people. Each post counts its own viewers, and the same person appearing in several posts is counted several times. The most that can be said accurately is that the largest single post was seen by 13,611 distinct viewers.
Net new followers
2. Across 63,701 views. Worth stating plainly rather than burying: very large reach produced almost no owned audience.

What is not counted here

A non-housing post
A link post to another section of this site drew 1,628 views in the same window. It is excluded from the totals above because it is not about the housing matter.
A music post
An unrelated music post drew 1,067 views in the same window. Also excluded.
Posts below the visible range
The analytics view was captured sorted by views. There is a gap in the captured range, and further posts sit below the last row recorded here. The totals above should therefore be read as a floor, not a complete count.

These figures are read by hand from the platform's own analytics and are not independently audited. Anyone quoting them is welcome to ask for the source screenshots.

pages.title: Who's involved
pages.kicker: Named where responsive, unnamed where not appropriate
pages.body:
Roma Britnell MP
Member for South West Coast. Responded 12 August 2026, encouraging and supportive. Making a ministerial representation on this matter.
Jacinta Ermacora MP
Member for Western Victoria. Contacted 6 August 2026. No response to date.
Salvos Connect
Caseworker support engaged throughout. Forwarded the specialist support letter independently.
Treating specialist
South West Healthcare. Provided the 12 August support letter and has been monitoring the health situation throughout.
Department response
A call and a follow-up email were received on 20 August 2026, the first substantive department contact after three prior office visits with no update given.

This record deliberately does not name individual departmental staff. The position throughout has been that this is a systems problem, not a person problem, several individuals in this process have been genuinely responsive, and the record should reflect that rather than obscure it.

pages.title: Status and next steps
pages.body:
14-20 Aug
DFFH's stated complaint response window ran, mostly unanswered despite repeated contact.
20 Aug
Window closed. A call and a follow-up email were received, the first substantive department contact in the process. A formal written response was dated this day.
21 Aug
The written response arrived by email. Two of the three questions raised are addressed: entitlement is one bedroom, and the two-bedroom property is said to be scheduled for extensive maintenance before going to the two-bedroom wait list. The third question, how long the property has stood empty, is not answered, and no maintenance date is given. The record is corrected accordingly: this was a response, not a silence.
The open question
The department's stated reason for refusing the two-bedroom property is that it is scheduled to undergo extensive maintenance before being offered to the two-bedroom wait list. No date has been given for those works. Three questions follow, and all three are answerable from the department's own records: on what date was the maintenance scheduled, is there a works order and what does it cover, and what works have been carried out at the property since February 2025. A property that received a reverse cycle unit, a new shower, repainted walls, laundry, tap, alarm and plumbing works during its last occupancy is not an obvious candidate for eighteen months of accumulated backlog while standing empty.
Two tracks now
The one-bedroom entitlement is a decision, and decisions have an internal appeal pathway which the letter itself sets out. The twelve-month gap between the April 2025 priority transfer process and the recorded April 2026 effective date, the rent deducted after exclusion, and three office visits with no update given, are questions of conduct. Conduct is the Ombudsman's jurisdiction. Merits are not. These are being pursued separately and should not be confused.
21 Aug
Victorian Ombudsman referral proceeding on conduct grounds. A meeting has also been offered with the department, in Warrnambool or via Salvos Connect. Commenting was also disabled overnight on the Koroit Community Notice Board post only, with the two Warrnambool group posts unaffected and still open. Existing comments there remain visible. No explanation given, and a single group closing replies on a single post is an ordinary administrator control.
Ongoing
This page will be updated as the complaint, the health record, and public reach develop. Nothing on this page is final.
Under consideration, not planned
A public gathering outside a regional DFFH office has been raised as a possible next step if the quieter channels, the complaint, the Ombudsman referral, media outreach, do not resolve this. Nothing organised, no date set, no commitment made. Listed here for the record, not as an announcement.

This is a live record, not a finished account. Figures, especially reach figures, will change. Check the "updated" date at the top of the page.

pages.title: Share your story
pages.body:
If this is happening to you too

Since 14 August, more than a dozen people have described the same wait, the same silence, and in several cases the exact same reasoning from the department, entirely independently of each other. That pattern is the strongest evidence on this whole record. If it's happening to you, it belongs here too.

This isn't run by, or affiliated with, DFFH or Homes Victoria. It's a public, factual record, built the same way the rest of this page is: sourced, correctable, and kept honest about what's confirmed and what isn't.

How this works

You choose how you're identified
First name only, anonymous, or a case number with no name at all. Your choice, asked before anything else.
You choose what it's used for
Published here, shared with journalists, referenced in a submission to the Victorian Ombudsman or Homes Victoria, reviewed by a small team helping run this record, or kept private and used for nothing beyond your own records. Each is its own separate choice.
Paraphrased, never altered
Long accounts may be shortened for the page. What you actually said is never changed in meaning, and nothing is attributed to circumstances you didn't describe.
Remove it any time
No reason needed. Message the details below.

What to include

Four things help most: when you first applied and under what category, what you were told the requirements were, what the process has actually been like, and, only if you want to, what it's costing you now. Dates and specifics matter more than anything else, they're what turns a story into a pattern.

Fill it in here
Or open it in its own tab
Open the form, useful on mobile if the embed renders awkwardly.
Or message directly
mahdagreenemoon@gmail.com
